summary: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to these modern challenges. We discuss the corrections for continuous scans and for multiple discrete tests, illustrated with simple numerical examples, and the interaction between ML and the LEE, which we connect to the broader literature on selective inference. We highlight open problems, including the computational cost of empirical calibration for complex models and the development of analytical shortcuts for ML test statistics, and offer recommendations for reporting discovery significance in both classical and ML-based searches in particle physics.

title: KEBBABS: Kilometric Enhanced Balloon-Baseline for Axion Birefringence Search
summary: We propose a broadband search for ultralight axion dark matter through the rotation of laser polarization induced by the axion--photon coupling. Two stratospheric balloons flying at altitudes of 30--40 km form a free-space optical link. One balloon sends a linearly polarized beam to the other, which reflects it back to a polarimeter on the first balloon. The long physical baseline provides an alternative to the repeated reflections used in resonant optical cavities. We target axion masses in the range $4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{eV}\lesssim m_a\lesssim10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. The lower edge corresponds to a frequency of about $1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, below which gondola roll about the line of sight can mimic a polarization signal. At $m_a=10^{-14}\,\mathrm{eV}$, a low-cost Pathfinder using flight-demonstrated technology could probe couplings as small as $g_{a\gamma}\simeq2.8\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, about a factor of two below the CAST bound. At the same mass, the Feasible today configuration could probe couplings just below the astrophysical bounds considered here, while the Futuristic configuration could reach $g_{a\gamma}\simeq6.4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, roughly two orders of magnitude below those bounds.

title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
summary: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

title: Machine Learning for Calabi--Yau Geometry and Heterotic Compactification
summary: Quantitative predictions from string compactification depend on geometric data that are difficult to compute analytically. This review surveys machine learning approaches to predicting topological properties of Calabi-Yau manifolds, discusses the search for new Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as numerical methods for approximating Ricci-flat metrics. In the context of heterotic compactifications, we explain how bundle metrics and harmonic matter forms enter calculations of canonically normalized Yukawa couplings and axion-matter interactions. We also outline applications to flux compactifications, warped and corrected backgrounds, and geometric structures beyond the Calabi-Yau setting. Finally, we review available datasets and software, highlight connections with analytic methods, and discuss geometric constraints, numerical validation, and recent progress in rigorous error control.

title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
summary: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.

title: Time-weighted energy correlators are infrared unsafe in gauge theories
summary: Energy correlators are infrared safe because each detector weights a parton by its energy, but a weight in the arrival time makes them infrared unsafe in gauge theories. For the state created by a scalar operator that makes two partons at lowest order in a weakly coupled conformal gauge theory, we show that the correlator of two time-weighted energy detectors (the light-ray operators $\int\!du\,u\,T_{uu}$) at separated directions diverges at two loops like the logarithm of the time window. The logarithm does not come from a single soft gluon, but from a soft parton pair with comparable energies, one parton in each detector; its coefficient is a closed-form function of the angle for any matter content. In $N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, we recover this coefficient from the two-gluon Regge term of the known four-point function and derive a simple relation to the logarithm in the charge correlator. In the planar theory the leading logarithms resum to a power of the window, set by the BFKL intercept.

title: Massive Triangle in Cosmological Correlator beyond Conformal Coupling
summary: A massive scalar coupled in pairs to the inflaton generates a one-loop primordial bispectrum whose mass corrections at generic momenta have lacked closed analytic expressions beyond conformal coupling. We obtain two leading mass corrections at arbitrary external momenta in terms of multiple polylogarithms of uniform weights three and four. Auxiliary-energy dressings preserve rational time integrals, revealing unexpected simplicity despite elliptic intermediate geometry. Independent full-loop evaluations, including blinded predictions, validate the closed forms. We also determine a subleading light-field singularity and recover the heavy-mass effective theory.

title: Resolving the Conformal Mode Problem with Einstein-Cartan Gravity
summary: We show that, when $\Lambda > 0$, the conformal factor problem is absent in first order Einstein-Cartan gravity in which the spin connection and tetrad are independent off-shell. At fixed connection, a conformal rescaling of the tetrad produces no conformal kinetic term so that the action is bounded from below. The original unbounded Einstein-Hilbert action, the Einstein-Hilbert action without the problematic conformal kinetic term and conformally invariant $R^{2}/\Lambda$ gravity arise as classical saddles of the Einstein-Cartan action with respect to the connection and conformal mode of the tetrad.

title: Quasinormal modes of black holes in astrophysical environments: Rainbow in the dark matter
summary: Matter around black holes affects the ringdown in two ways: through the background geometry and through the response of the matter itself. We compute axial and polar gravitational quasinormal modes of a black hole embedded in a relativistic Hernquist-type dark matter halo, following the fundamental mode and the first three overtones associated with the vacuum Schwarzschild spectrum. The polar sector couples metric and matter perturbations. At small halo compactness, both sectors follow the familiar gravitational redshift law. Most of the departure from the typical redshift at larger compactness is accounted for by the exact horizon lapse factor of the background. The remaining residual departure to this lapse is sector dependent. Axial and polar frequencies are split, with their splitting growing from the fundamental through the third overtone. At large halo compactness the split grows by an order of magnitude, while overtone-to-fundamental frequency ratios depart from a common rescaling. Within the adopted dark matter profile, the halo acts on the ringdown as a prism that disperses the gravitational spectrum, leaving a parity-dependent imprint that no common rescaling of the frequencies can reproduce. Parity-isospectrality is, thus, broken.

title: Hamiltonian approach to isospectrality in nonrotating black holes
summary: In this work, we revisit the isospectrality of black hole perturbations from a Hamiltonian perspective. For a nonrotating, uncharged system, we present a convenient canonical description of the background degrees of freedom that facilitates comparison with the usual Lagrangian formulation. This allows us to identify phase-space counterparts of the superpotential and the algebraically special modes and show that they satisfy the expected isospectral relations, at least on shell or off shell modulo some subtle lapse redefinitions. Finally, we investigate the extent to which these results persist in theories that effectively modify general relativity. In this setting, we formally quantify the corresponding deviations from the classical relations and the associated potential violations of isospectrality to first order in the modifications.

title: Modular fluctuation relations on local causal horizons
summary: Local causal horizons provide a setting for studying horizon thermodynamics in the neighborhood of any regular spacetime point. Here, we investigate this description beyond mean energy and entropy balances by studying fluctuations of boost-energy transfer induced by unitary perturbations of the horizon reference state. Using the modular structure of the horizon algebra and a thermal reference state, we construct an energy transfer probability measure and derive integral and detailed fluctuation relations with the mean entropy production being expressed in terms of the Araki relative entropy. The formulation accommodates type-III algebras without introducing a reduced density matrix and can be extended to global bifurcate Killing horizons admitting the required thermal reference state. For coherent scalar-field perturbations, we obtain a closed form for the characteristic function, identify the mean transfer with the excess boost-energy flux, and derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounding the variance in terms of the mean transfer. We then explore the geometric implications by postulating a stochastic horizon entropy--area correspondence that associates an area change with each counted energy transfer. Under this additional hypothesis, we obtain fluctuation relations for area changes and an area change uncertainty bound for coherent perturbations.

title: Low-latency gravitational wave alert infrastructure and new data products for multi-messenger astronomy during LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's fourth observing run
summary: Multi-messenger investigations of compact object mergers, such as binary neutron star and neutron star-black hole systems, remain among the most dynamic frontiers of modern astronomy. During the fourth observing run of Advanced LIGO, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA, the search for joint electromagnetic and neutrino counterparts to gravitational-wave signals continued using public, semi-automated data products distributed in near real-time. The sky localizations and preliminary source characterizations provided by these alerts helped guide multiple rapid follow-up observations to candidate gravitational-wave events. During this run, the low-latency search parameter space was expanded to include the sub-solar mass regime and associated public data products were developed. Further, chirp mass estimates of the binary merger system were introduced as a new public data product and distributed to enable follow-up searches to concentrate their resources on the most promising transients. In order to streamline the implementation of new searches and data products, a mock data challenge, known as the Low-Latency Production Integration Challenge (LLPIC), was used as a replay of a simulated population of gravitational-wave sources to optimize and profile the software infrastructure and scientific deliverables. In this paper we describe these new public data products, their performance and the result of end-to-end testing of the low-latency infrastructure with the LLPIC.

title: Environmental resonances in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals within boson clouds
summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) offer a promising probe of matter environments around massive black holes through gravitational-wave (GW) observations. We investigate orbital resonances induced by conservative gravitational perturbations from such environments. Combining a multiparameter expansion with the action-angle formalism, we derive a general resonance condition for generic bound Kerr orbits. Applying this framework to ultralight scalar clouds formed through black hole superradiance, we show that orbital resonances can arise from a single-mode cloud without requiring transitions between cloud modes. Our analysis demonstrates that these resonances can lead to significant GW dephasing, providing a new avenue for probing boson clouds through GWs and highlighting the importance of including environmental resonances in accurate EMRI waveform modeling.

title: Cosmographic Analysis of Gravitational Baryogenesis in Running-$G$ Cosmology
summary: Gravitational baryogenesis produces a baryon asymmetry through the coupling of the baryon current to the derivative of the Ricci scalar, so its yield is set by the expansion history around decoupling. We study this mechanism in cosmology with a running Newton coupling of the asymptotic-safety type. Writing the Ricci scalar and its derivative through the Hubble rate, the deceleration parameter $q$ and the jerk $j$, we show that the yield is proportional to the kernel $K=2+q-j$, which vanishes for radiation in general relativity, and to a power of an enhancement factor measuring how strongly the running coupling accelerates the expansion at decoupling. We treat hybrid, intermediate, logamediate, emergent, bouncing and little-rip scale factors and determine where the observed asymmetry is reproduced for the $J^\mu\partial_\mu R$ and $J^\mu\partial_\mu R^2$ couplings; a table compares the six cases.

title: An Electromagnetic Ergoregion Limits the Reconnection-Driven Penrose Process
summary: Magnetic reconnection taps black-hole rotational energy via negative-energy ejecta, but field geometry itself can forbid such ejection inside the spacetime ergoregion. We identify a covariant electromagnetic (EM) ergoregion for general degenerate, magnetically dominated fields in stationary spacetimes. Outside the EM ergoregion, even ultrarelativistic field-guided ejecta cannot attain negative Killing energy. For Alfvénic reconnection outflows, the magnetization threshold scales inversely with the transverse distance to the EM ergosurface. The mass-loaded Kerr model places the EM ergosurface at about 75% of the radial interval from the horizon to the spacetime ergosurface, close to the time-averaged boundary inferred from a dynamical simulation. Together, these results show that field geometry determines where negative-energy ejection is possible, while magnetization sets the threshold for realizing it.

title: Kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
summary: Investigating black hole physics in semi-classical gravitational theory is an interesting and important direction. When the backreaction of the conformal anomaly-induced effective stress-energy tensor is taken into account, the black hole spacetime can be largely altered which changes many properties of the black hole. In this work, rather than restricting our attention to the type-A anomaly, we incorporate the type-B anomaly and investigate how it modifies the spacetime structure obtained when only the type-A anomaly is considered. We find that for a specific relation between the central charges and the cosmological constant, the semiclassical Einstein equations can be solved analytically, yielding a metric that takes the exact form of the Kiselev black hole. After deriving the solution, we further discuss the properties of this new black hole solutions. Our work serves as an essential stepping stone for studying black hole geometries under the full conformal anomaly.

title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
summary: We investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub--NUT spacetime in the sector with vanishing Kerr rotation. We recover its normalized metric from the Plebański--Demiański family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon Killing directions through the large-companion limit. The black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective Killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar Gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-I accelerating Taub--NUT solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. We establish separability of the type-D null Hamilton--Jacobi equation and construct an unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams. We also examine axial identifications and chronology-violating regions. The resulting geometrical and dynamical distinctions clarify how the two accelerating NUT families differ despite sharing their nonaccelerating and zero-NUT limits; the radial atlas is not claimed to be a unique maximal four-dimensional extension.

title: Lorentz charges for Lovelock gravity
summary: In this paper, we construct the charges associated with the residual local Lorentz transformations on a black hole horizon in the Lovelock class of theories of gravity. The horizons is assumed to be non- expanding horizons, \emph{i.e} a null hypersurface for which the expansion corresponding to the null generator vanish. Naturally, these hypersurfaces preserve only a subgroup of the full Lorentz group of the bulk, and the residual symmetries correspond to the little group which stabilizes the horizon null generator. We show that on the horizon, the Hamiltonian charge corresponding to the residual local Lorentz boost is the Wald entropy.

title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
summary: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

title: Semiclassical causal geodesics: Schwarzschild spacetime case
summary: We propose an extension of the integral quantization, applied previously to the semiclassical description of a test particle in the flat Minkowski spacetime, to the Schwarzschild spacetime. This extension yields a local integral quantization. We calculate the transition amplitudes between coherent states of a particle in a mass layer, which effectively leads to a Klein-Gordon-type dynamics. The calculated probability distributions reproduce locally the classical radial geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime. The local integral quantization presented here seems to be applicable to semiclassical quantization of geodesic motion in other curved spacetimes.

title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
summary: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrt{\Lambda}/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $\Lambda > 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $\Lambda>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

title: phenjax: the IMRPhenomT waveform family in JAX for accelerated analyses on CPUs and GPUs
summary: We present phenjax, a JAX implementation of the precessing time-domain IMRPhenomT family of models for the gravitational wave signal emitted in compact binary coalescence. The code keeps the structure of its reference Python implementation, phenomxpy, and reproduces, on average, its polarizations to a few $\times 10^{-12}$ of the peak strain for all the models, aligned-spin and precessing. The waveform models now take advantage of the JAX construction: compiled once per array shape, vectorized over events (batching), differentiable and executed on CPUs or GPUs with the same source code. Different additional features address the cost of long signals and of heterogeneous populations in a batch. On one NVIDIA H100, for the precessing TPHM model on LISA-mass populations, phenjax is 3 to 6 times faster than phenomxpy when both codes evaluate one event at a time and 20 to 30 times faster when phenjax evaluates the events in batches of 8. We estimate that, for waveform generation, one GPU does the work of 1300 to 2700 cores of a current CPU node at 25 to 45 times less energy per waveform. As a backend of a global-fit LISA massive black hole pipeline, performed on the Sangria dataset, phenjax recovers the same posteriors as the other waveform backends at a lower computational cost. In a comparison with phentax, the wall time was 13 minutes instead of 21.

title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
comment: 23 pages; minor corrections; additional details on the Pfaffian factorization of \(g_n\) and on GCD have been added
summary: We obtain a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori solutions to the Ernst equation. The main consequence of this result is the proof of Nakamura's conjecture relating the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model, presented in arXiv:2611.19558.

title: A proof of Nakamura's conjecture
summary: We prove Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the 2D Toda model and solutions of the Ernst equation, using the Pfaffian solutions obtained in our previous work arXiv:2610.27420.

title: The black hole IR triangle for scalar QED
summary: We construct the black hole infrared triangle of scalar QED on a stretched Schwarzschild horizon at tree level. In the covariant phase space of the near-horizon Maxwell field, the soft charge is a corner term. The memory is the zero mode of the gauge-invariant radiative field along the generators. It is conjugate to the boundary gauge mode that labels the degenerate horizon vacua, and Gauss' law fixes it by the flux of charge through the horizon. The Noether flux of the residual gauge transformation through the stretched horizon is not conserved by the scattering, because charged matter crosses the stretched horizon in both directions. The flux with its matter part removed is the soft charge, which generates the large gauge transformation. Its Ward identity is equivalent to a soft photon theorem in every radiative partial wave, which we derive from the near-horizon Feynman rules and, where these do not control the emission, from the field equations at leading order. The main difference from null infinity is that on a stretched horizon both radial branches of the field are independent boundary data. The hard charge is a radial flux. With both branches present it weights each leg by the direction of its radial motion, and the soft factor is a sign per leg. The endpoint data on the two branches give two boundary observables, the time-integrated transverse magnetic and electric fields. The field radiated by a scattering process contributes only to the first, where it cancels the change in the Coulomb memory of the charges, so that the soft charge is conserved. A charge that crosses the horizon enters both. We also discuss the infrared divergence, the dressing of the external states, and the fate of the memory in the Hartle--Hawking state, where it performs a random walk driven by the Hawking radiation.

title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
summary: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

title: Bounds on Love Numbers and Quasinormal Modes from the Surface Impedance
summary: The surface impedance of a body is fixed by its interior alone and encodes its entire tidal response. We derive bounds on Love numbers and quasinormal modes from constraints on the impedance that follow from either of two properties of a stable body: it is lossless, meaning that it dissipates no energy, or it is passive, meaning that it never gives back more energy than it has received. For a lossless body, every dynamical Love number is bounded from above and below, exactly in general relativity, in any renormalization scheme and at any scale. Earlier bounds are exact for Newtonian stars but fail for compact stars, because they take the response to arbitrarily fast tides to be zero or non-negative, whereas in general relativity it is negative. The quasinormal modes of a lossless body are also excluded from a region of the complex frequency plane set by the mass and radius. Each known Love number enlarges the excluded region. Conversely, the quasinormal modes bound each Love number from below, given the lower ones. For a passive body of horizon scale, such as a black hole, the static Love number lies in a window that closes onto the vanishing black-hole value as the body's surface approaches the horizon.

title: Chaotic singularities inside vacuum black holes
summary: According to the conjecture of Belinski, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz, general relativity gives rise to chaotic dynamics in the vicinity of generic spacelike singularities. However, no vacuum black hole has been shown to exhibit this behaviour. Here we construct stationary, asymptotically locally AdS$_5$ black holes with regular, triaxially squashed horizons and causal exteriors, whose homogeneous interiors realize the cosmological billiard of generic five-dimensional vacuum gravity. We identify a simple algebraic condition on the horizon data that is necessary for the interior billiard to be chaotic, and show that solutions with regular horizons locally access an open set of billiard trajectories.

title: Divergence-type hydrodynamics of radial oscillations in viscous neutron stars
summary: Based on a simplified model of a viscous neutron star in the Newtonian limit coupled to a quadratic dissipative fluid theory of divergence type with bulk viscosity only, we explore the impact of nonlinear effects on the evolution of radial perturbations, and compare it with the results of linear hydrodynamics. For high values of the bulk viscosity $\zeta_B \gtrsim 5\times 10^{31}$ g/cm/s, the linear theory develops growing oscillations, which do appear in the quadratic theory but at much higher values of $\zeta_B$. The quadratic theory shows stronger damping of oscillations, longer decay rates of non-hydrodynamic modes and also a ``stiffer'' evolution of radial perturbations that results in less deformation. These results suggest that nonlinear effects may be relevant to capture the dynamics of the long-lived non-hydrodynamic modes present at high $\zeta_B$.

title: All known supersymmetric $\mathrm{AdS}_4 \times S^7$ uplifts from maximal supergravity
summary: The solutions of $D=4$ $\mathcal N=8$ SO(8)-gauged supergravity uplift consistently to eleven dimensions. All known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua of this theory lie in an $\mathcal N=1$ truncation containing seven chiral multiplets. In this paper, we work out the uplift of this seven-chiral sector, providing a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ solutions in this class. We then specialise to the $\mathcal N=1$ vacua with U(1)$^2$ and SO(3) symmetry, obtain their new $D=11$ uplifts and bring out their internal geometries. Both of them admit a Kaluza--Klein-type description. For the U(1)$^2$ solution, this uses the global Hopf fibration of $S^7$ over $\mathbb{CP}^3$. One U(1) acts on the fibre, while the other generates the only continuous isometry of the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^3$ base. For the SO(3) solution, the geometry takes a local non-abelian Kaluza--Klein form, with SO(3) acting on the fibres and no residual continuous symmetry on the four-dimensional base.

title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
summary: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. We find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. The former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. Second, we compute the growth rate of the Krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the IR. In particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

title: The Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems and curved spacetimes - An orthonormal frames approach
comment: 28 pages, 1 figure; general treatment of the Dirac equation (in the absence of torsion) for cases in which $γ^{\hat 0}$ serves as the hermitizing matrix for the Dirac matrices
summary: In this pedagogical article we discuss the Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems. We explain the need for connections when dealing with spinor fields and present the practical steps needed to compute the Dirac operator in a general setting, allowing for arbitrary coordinate systems and position-dependent orthonormal gamma matrices, both of which can simplify computations in certain scenarios. The extension to include minimally coupled gravity is straightforward. Examples are provided, including constructing the Dirac equation in spherical and cylindrical symmetry (with or without gravity) and the Kerr spacetime. We also briefly comment on the advantages and disadvantages of various tetrads and orthonormal gamma matrices. This manuscript should be accessible to readers who have studied the Dirac equation at an introductory level (e.g., in Cartesian coordinates in flat spacetime with constant gamma matrices). The emphasis is on the use of orthonormal frames, since these correspond to the coordinate systems most familiar to readers when dealing with most field theories, and represent the physical frames where measurements are performed. The aim is to get the reader quickly to the point of being able to do calculations, so the presentation favors a concise, pragmatic approach over extended derivations.

title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
summary: We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.

title: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
summary: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.

title: Entanglement and HBAR entropy in a Lorentzian non-commutative black hole
summary: We investigate how Lorentzian non-commutative smearing affects entanglement and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) outside a black hole. For a massless scalar field, tracing over the interior partner gives the exterior quantum channel, its logarithmic negativity, mutual information, and Bell entanglement fidelity. At fixed mass and Killing frequency, increasing the smearing lowers the surface gravity, increases the accessible correlations, and suppresses the leading atomic emission probability. The horizon displacement begins at order $\sqrt{\Theta}$, while the thermal correction at infinity begins at order $\Theta$. At fixed local frequency, the redshift introduces a term of order $\sqrt{\Theta}$ at fixed areal radius. Holding the proper distance fixed, it cancels this term and recovers the common Rindler response close to the horizon. For a freely falling atom, emission and absorption obey detailed balance at the Hawking temperature in the leading horizon approximation. Random atomic injection drives the selected mode from the vacuum to a thermal state with an exact relaxation law and nonnegative entropy production. Near equilibrium, we obtain $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/4$ when the radiated energy is drawn from horizon heat, where $\dot A_p$ is the positive radiative area loss. When the radiation is assigned to ADM mass loss at fixed smearing length $\ell=4\sqrt{\Theta/\pi}$, the result is $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/[4(1-\ell/r_+)]$. The mass dependence of the exterior source thus enters the entropy per unit area lost at order $\sqrt{\Theta}$.

title: A Pole-Cut Formula for Holographic Extremal Correlators
summary: We show that the holographic spectral function of a neutral massless scalar on the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black brane in $AdS_5$ admits an elegant formula in terms of the quasi-normal modes (QNMs) and branch-cut data. In the extremal case, the spectral data comprises the zeros of the boundary source function, i.e. the QNMs, as well as its phase discontinuity across the branch cut on the negative imaginary axis of the complex frequency plane. This formula neatly factorizes into an infinite product over the QNM poles and a factor encoding the branch cut discontinuity. We derive this pole-cut formula as the zero-temperature limit of the QNM product formula for holographic thermal correlators, with the branch-cut contribution arising from the coalescence of the QNMs on the negative imaginary axis. We also clarify the role of the near-horizon $AdS_2$ region in this context. Consistency with the OPE of the boundary correlator provides extremal sum-rules involving both the QNMs as well as the phase discontinuity function. We also find that this holographic consistency forces the asymptotic form of the QNMs to be related to the asymptotics of the phase discontinuity function. We verify our formula and these OPE constraints numerically. We also demonstrate that, in the time domain, the pole and cut factors each produce complex-time singularities, whose location is determined by the optical distance between the boundary and the black-brane singularity. We expect the pole-cut factorization structure of spectral functions to hold for more general fluctuations of extremal black branes.

title: Massive Triangle in Cosmological Correlator beyond Conformal Coupling
summary: A massive scalar coupled in pairs to the inflaton generates a one-loop primordial bispectrum whose mass corrections at generic momenta have lacked closed analytic expressions beyond conformal coupling. We obtain two leading mass corrections at arbitrary external momenta in terms of multiple polylogarithms of uniform weights three and four. Auxiliary-energy dressings preserve rational time integrals, revealing unexpected simplicity despite elliptic intermediate geometry. Independent full-loop evaluations, including blinded predictions, validate the closed forms. We also determine a subleading light-field singularity and recover the heavy-mass effective theory.

title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
summary: We propose a background independent quantization of vacuum general relativity on four dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes. Starting from first order gravity, we solve the gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion and obtain the reduced phase space at finite $G_N$. We promote its canonical Poisson brackets to commutation relations and use deformations of the reduced action to define an algebra of observables. Equipped with this, we use Gaussian wavefunctions of canonical pairs to construct a nonperturbative Hilbert space representation, for which this algebra generates a type I factor. By composing amplitudes between states prepared on null cones, we then obtain a Lorentzian path integral in which each sum over intermediate states converges absolutely. As a check, we compute the amplitude for graviton pair creation and annihilation on a null cone nonperturbatively in $G_N$ and find a finite closed form expression, even though expanding first in $G_N$ yields a logarithmic divergence. We next use diffeomorphism invariance of the path integral to show that a macroscopic causal diamond with a given maximum size has a finite dimensional Hilbert space. From the Lorentzian trace we obtain the Bekenstein Hawking entropy for marginally trapped surfaces and calculate its logarithmic correction for large Schwarzschild black holes, recovering at one loop the coefficient Sen obtained through Euclidean methods. We end by deriving the semiclassical Einstein equations to one loop as the low energy limit of this theory.

title: Proceedings of "Accelerating ALICE background simulations: A WGAN Approach to slow-neutron induced TPC loopers" CHEP 2026, 26/05/2026
authors: Andreas Morsch for the ALICE Collaboration
summary: The simulation of background processes in high-energy physics can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. To provide the most realistic data description at the ALICE experiment using Monte Carlo simulations, we investigated alternative solutions to generate the products of electromagnetic interactions initiated by slow neutrons in the Time Projection Chamber (TPC). Specifically, electrons and positrons from these processes can spiral repeatedly within the magnetic field in the detector (so-called "loopers") and tracking them via full transport frameworks, such as GEANT4, requires extensive computing resources. A fast simulation framework based on a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) was developed to speed up the simulation process. Our solution is designed to bypass the significant computational cost associated with transporting neutrons to low energies by directly generating the kinematic properties (e.g., momentum, production vertex) of the resulting electron-positron pairs (from neutron capture) and electrons from Compton scattering. The generative model successfully reproduces the complex multidimensional distributions of the background tracks with high fidelity, maintaining agreement with the full GEANT4 simulation. By replacing the full transport of these specific background components with the WGAN inference, a tenfold speedup is achieved, making the simulation of loopers a negligible component of the total processing time. Moreover, the fast simulation framework is modular, allowing for the future inclusion of other background sources, such as nuclear spallation products.

title: Ratio of $\barΛ$ to $K_\rm{S}^0$ production cross-sections in $pp$ collisions at 13.6TeV
comment: All figures and tables, along with machine-readable versions and any supplementary material and additional information, are available at this https URL
summary: The production cross-section ratio of promptly produced $\bar{\Lambda}$ and $K_\rm{S}^0$ hadrons is measured in proton-proton collision data at a centre-of-mass energy of 13.6TeV recorded in 2024 with the upgraded LHCb detector and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $64\rm{pb}^{-1}$. The ratio is presented as a function of transverse momentum, $p_\rm{T}$, and rapidity, $y$, in the ranges $0.15 < p_\rm{T} < 2.5\rm{GeV}/c$ and $2.0 < y < 4.5$. The results are in good agreement with previous measurements at different centre-of-mass energies. They are compared to predictions from currently available event generators and can be used as input in future event generator tunings.

title: Letter of Intent: AN Underground Belayed In-Shaft (ANUBIS) detector
summary: Long-lived particles (LLPs) arise naturally in many extensions of the Standard Model, notably in models with dark matter candidates or motivated by baryogenesis. LLPs produced at or above the electroweak scale with decay lengths of tens of metres escape the general-purpose LHC detectors and cannot be produced at sufficient rates in forward and beam-dump experiments. This Letter of Intent proposes the ANUBIS detector, which would instrument the ceiling of the ATLAS cavern and the bottom of its access shafts with about 1600~m$^2$ of resistive plate chambers in two tracking layers about 1~m apart, using the air-filled volume above the ATLAS detector as decay volume. The ANUBIS detector exploits the full ATLAS event information to suppress backgrounds, and exchanges triggers with the ATLAS experiment. With 3~ab$^{-1}$ at the High-Luminosity LHC, it would improve the sensitivity to exotic Higgs-boson decays into long-lived scalars by two to three orders of magnitude, probe heavy neutral leptons of all three flavours down to mixings of about $2\times10^{-8}$, and extend the reach for axion-like particles. The \textsl{pro}ANUBIS demonstrator, operated in the ATLAS cavern in 2024 and 2025, has validated the detector technology. The detector design, trigger concept, integration with the ATLAS experiment and a timeline towards installation in LHC Long Shutdown 4 are presented.

title: Lower Bound on the Lightest Neutrino Mass with Resonant Neutrino Self-Interactions
summary: We show the possibility of using the resonant $s$-channel scattering of ultra high energy astrophysical neutrinos with the low energy cosmic neutrino background to put a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass. This can be realized and illustrated by neutrino self-interactions with a light scalar mediator of $\mathcal O(1)$ MeV mass. After analyzing the kinematics and cross section features of the $s$-channel resonance, we derive from first principles the double transport equations with double regeneration terms for the coupled evolution of neutrinos and anti-neutrinos. The simulated event spectrum is then compared with the HESE 7.5 year data observed at IceCube to give a clear lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass.

title: Probing the CKM Origin of CP Violation with Paramagnetic EDMs and Rare Kaon Decays
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, plus 16 pages of Supplemental Material
summary: In the Standard Model, paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are dominated by kaon exchange, which pairs the CP-violating short-distance transition $s\to d\,e^+e^-$ with a CP-conserving weak kaon-nucleon coupling. Long-distance two-photon exchange, which dominates $K_L\to e^+e^-$, gives an electron vertex about thirty-five times larger than the short-distance one and could obscure this origin. We show that it does not: the two-photon vertex conserves CP and must be paired with the CP-violating penguin component of the nucleon coupling, whose relative size is $3\times10^{-4}$, so that electromagnetic corrections stay at the few-percent level. Paramagnetic EDMs therefore measure $\mathrm{Im}(V_{ts}^*V_{td})$ and, together with the CP-violating $S$ wave of $K_S\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and $K_L\to\pi^0\nu\bar\nu$, determine the same imaginary coordinate of a kaon CKM plane with electrons, muons, and neutrinos, without $B$-decay input. Lepton-specific new physics, or CP violation that bypasses kaon exchange, would separate these determinations. Testing their common CKM origin calls for coordinated progress in molecular EDM searches, rare-kaon experiments at LHCb, NA62, and KOTO, and lattice determinations of weak nucleon matrix elements.

title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
summary: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to these modern challenges. We discuss the corrections for continuous scans and for multiple discrete tests, illustrated with simple numerical examples, and the interaction between ML and the LEE, which we connect to the broader literature on selective inference. We highlight open problems, including the computational cost of empirical calibration for complex models and the development of analytical shortcuts for ML test statistics, and offer recommendations for reporting discovery significance in both classical and ML-based searches in particle physics.

title: Quantum critical collapse to an extremal black hole
summary: It has been emphasized recently that some extremal black holes are "critical" solutions, lying at the threshold between gravitational collapse and dispersion. We study the effect of quantum gravity on critical solutions for the collapse of a thin shell of charged dust. We consider the Hamiltonian that generates the shell equation of motion with respect to the exterior Killing time and coincides with the ADM energy on-shell. Near criticality, this Hamiltonian is shown to be canonically equivalent to that of a Liouville theory with negative potential. After quantization, this model predicts that a collapsing shell has a non-trivial probability of undergoing a quantum mechanical bounce when its energy above extremality is comparable to the "breakdown scale". The bounce probability approaches unity at extremality. Hence this model predicts that the critical surface in the classical theory is thickened quantum mechanically into a "critical layer". The probability density function for the black hole energy is suppressed below the breakdown scale in the same way as found recently by Turiaci and Wu.

title: The black hole IR triangle for scalar QED
summary: We construct the black hole infrared triangle of scalar QED on a stretched Schwarzschild horizon at tree level. In the covariant phase space of the near-horizon Maxwell field, the soft charge is a corner term. The memory is the zero mode of the gauge-invariant radiative field along the generators. It is conjugate to the boundary gauge mode that labels the degenerate horizon vacua, and Gauss' law fixes it by the flux of charge through the horizon. The Noether flux of the residual gauge transformation through the stretched horizon is not conserved by the scattering, because charged matter crosses the stretched horizon in both directions. The flux with its matter part removed is the soft charge, which generates the large gauge transformation. Its Ward identity is equivalent to a soft photon theorem in every radiative partial wave, which we derive from the near-horizon Feynman rules and, where these do not control the emission, from the field equations at leading order. The main difference from null infinity is that on a stretched horizon both radial branches of the field are independent boundary data. The hard charge is a radial flux. With both branches present it weights each leg by the direction of its radial motion, and the soft factor is a sign per leg. The endpoint data on the two branches give two boundary observables, the time-integrated transverse magnetic and electric fields. The field radiated by a scattering process contributes only to the first, where it cancels the change in the Coulomb memory of the charges, so that the soft charge is conserved. A charge that crosses the horizon enters both. We also discuss the infrared divergence, the dressing of the external states, and the fate of the memory in the Hartle--Hawking state, where it performs a random walk driven by the Hawking radiation.

title: The OPE of lines beyond CFT
summary: We discuss the fusion of parallel line defects in theories defined by relevant deformations of a conformal fixed point. We propose an operator product expansion to describe this limit in terms of a Wilsonian effective action whose coefficients are computable in conformal perturbation theory around the UV. This allows one to fix, order by order, the fusion limit of correlation functions involving the defects, up to non-perturbative coefficients associated to correlation functions (condensates) on the fused defect. It thus generalizes the familiar OPE of local operators in QFT. As a non-perturbative test of our proposal, we consider the short-distance potential between two magnetic impurities in the $2d$ Ising model. We find excellent agreement between the OPE framework and DMRG extractions of the potential and condensates (the latter also computed exactly with integrability). In addition, we consider a number of solvable models to illustrate different features of the framework.

title: The String Theory Photinoverse
summary: Type-IIB string compactifications typically give rise to a significant number of RR-photons. These are generically massless and do not possess any light charged states, making them `superhidden'. However, since supersymmetry is present at least at some high scale, corresponding `dark photinos' are also predicted. The kinetic mixing of the photons together with the SUSY breaking mass terms of the photinos makes the latter observable. We identify geometries in which the mixing is induced by Wilson lines and show that their expectation values are generically non-zero. As a result, most of the dark photinos, which are lighter than the visible sector SUSY breaking scale, mix significantly with the bino and hence couple to the Standard Model sufficiently strongly to leave potentially observable traces. In particular, volume modulus and inflaton decays generically induce a cosmological abundance of dark photinos that can explain dark matter. We find that the `natural Photinoverse dark matter parameter space' is already accessible to current experiments, notably gamma ray observations, which therefore have discovery potential in the near future.

title: Gauge groups of type 0 orientifolds
summary: We determine the global form of the gauge groups of the orthogonal and symplectic type 0 orientifolds, using the constraints from perturbative and brane states. In the process, we correct some misprints in type 0 vacuum amplitudes that have propagated in the literature. For type 0A, our analysis reveals a parity condition on the numbers of D9-branes in the orthogonal orientifold and a puzzle concerning the decay of a tachyonic D0-brane in the symplectic orientifold.

title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
summary: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

title: Neural Network Field Theory and the AdS/CFT Correspondence
comment: 69 pages, comments and references are welcome
summary: We develop a neural realization of massive scalar field theory on Euclidean anti--de Sitter space and its holographic boundary observables within neural network field theory (NN--FT). We construct Fourier--Bessel cosine neurons whose covariance reproduces the regulated massive AdS propagator exactly at finite network width, with the Gaussian field theory recovered in the infinite-width limit. We introduce quartic interactions through two complementary approaches. The first implements a prescribed interaction by deforming the neural parameter measure, while the second generates a local quartic interaction from the statistics of auxiliary binary neurons. Applying the BDHM prescription directly to the neural ensemble, we recover the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, the conformal boundary two-point function, and the leading connected four-point contact Witten diagram. We further show that distinct neural architectures can reproduce the same leading boundary correlators while defining inequivalent bulk theories. These results establish a framework for studying interacting scalar holography within NN--FT and clarify the role of neural architecture in encoding bulk dynamics and boundary observables.

title: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal two-dimensional CFTs
comment: 66 pages + appendices, 19 figures, 1 table; comments and references are welcome
summary: In this work, we study local operator quenches in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories with complex-time evolution, which can be viewed as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system interacting with an environment. In contrast to quenches of the vacuum, the thermal initial state allows several conformal families to participate in the evolution. We show that their competition can produce cascades of approximately homogeneous energy plateaux, with successive plateaux approaching the energies of different primary states. Using conformal Ward identities on the cylinder and torus, we determine the local energy density and illustrate this behavior in free-field theories, the Ising model and Wess--Zumino--Witten models. We develop a cold-limit spectral description in which the dominant primary channel determines the height of each plateau, while conformal dimensions and operator matrix elements govern the transitions between them. For a fixed compact unitary CFT, we show that only finitely many primary channels can contribute to the leading plateau sequence. Finally, we discuss the large-central-charge regime, relating light-operator plateaux to few-particle sectors in thermal AdS and examining the limitations of this picture for heavy quenches.

title: Bounds on Love Numbers and Quasinormal Modes from the Surface Impedance
summary: The surface impedance of a body is fixed by its interior alone and encodes its entire tidal response. We derive bounds on Love numbers and quasinormal modes from constraints on the impedance that follow from either of two properties of a stable body: it is lossless, meaning that it dissipates no energy, or it is passive, meaning that it never gives back more energy than it has received. For a lossless body, every dynamical Love number is bounded from above and below, exactly in general relativity, in any renormalization scheme and at any scale. Earlier bounds are exact for Newtonian stars but fail for compact stars, because they take the response to arbitrarily fast tides to be zero or non-negative, whereas in general relativity it is negative. The quasinormal modes of a lossless body are also excluded from a region of the complex frequency plane set by the mass and radius. Each known Love number enlarges the excluded region. Conversely, the quasinormal modes bound each Love number from below, given the lower ones. For a passive body of horizon scale, such as a black hole, the static Love number lies in a window that closes onto the vanishing black-hole value as the body's surface approaches the horizon.

title: Chaotic singularities inside vacuum black holes
summary: According to the conjecture of Belinski, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz, general relativity gives rise to chaotic dynamics in the vicinity of generic spacelike singularities. However, no vacuum black hole has been shown to exhibit this behaviour. Here we construct stationary, asymptotically locally AdS$_5$ black holes with regular, triaxially squashed horizons and causal exteriors, whose homogeneous interiors realize the cosmological billiard of generic five-dimensional vacuum gravity. We identify a simple algebraic condition on the horizon data that is necessary for the interior billiard to be chaotic, and show that solutions with regular horizons locally access an open set of billiard trajectories.

title: RMT${}_2$: Random Spectral Correlations for CFT${}_2$ and AdS${}_3$ Gravity
summary: We present the full framework of RMT${}_2$, a consistent unification of random matrix theory and modular invariance. The systematic prescription, which augments the existing construction by incorporating spin, lifts random matrix correlators to $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ Poincaré sums of their Mellin transforms, in a manner which enforces random matrix correlations near extremality in every spinning primary sector. The resulting RMT${}_2$ correlators are further expressible in terms of an orthogonal basis of Eisenstein series and Maass cusp forms. We demonstrate the construction by lifting the two-point correlators at arbitrary genus of the Airy model, in both unitary and orthogonal symmetry classes, exhibiting the modular-invariant topological expansion of RMT${}_2$; a resummation of the genus expansion shows that the modular-invariant spectral form factor preserves the ramp-plateau structure. Holographically, RMT${}_2$ provides a concrete benchmark and explicit candidate expressions for comparison with off-shell wormhole amplitudes in AdS${}_3$ gravity, with any number of torus boundaries. We explicitly compute the universal RMT${}_2$ three-point correlator, corresponding to the putative three-boundary wormhole.

title: Machine Learning for Calabi--Yau Geometry and Heterotic Compactification
summary: Quantitative predictions from string compactification depend on geometric data that are difficult to compute analytically. This review surveys machine learning approaches to predicting topological properties of Calabi-Yau manifolds, discusses the search for new Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as numerical methods for approximating Ricci-flat metrics. In the context of heterotic compactifications, we explain how bundle metrics and harmonic matter forms enter calculations of canonically normalized Yukawa couplings and axion-matter interactions. We also outline applications to flux compactifications, warped and corrected backgrounds, and geometric structures beyond the Calabi-Yau setting. Finally, we review available datasets and software, highlight connections with analytic methods, and discuss geometric constraints, numerical validation, and recent progress in rigorous error control.

title: On the Structure Constants of ${\cal N}=2$ Liouville Theory
summary: We show the structure constants of $\mathcal{N}=2$ spacelike Liouville theory. The absence of self-duality under $b\leftrightarrow b^{-1}$, where $b$ is the Liouville coupling, prevents a straightforward application of the standard bootstrap methods used in $\mathcal{N}=0$ and $\mathcal{N}=1$ Liouville theory. Motivated by the fermionic FZZ duality with the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})/U(1)$ supercoset theory, we establish an algebraic correspondence between the two theories, including a matching of their null vectors. We then derive the three-point structure constants in superspace. The neutral sector structure constants are associated with the spectral-flow-preserving structure constant of the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model, while the two charged sectors correspond to its spectral-flow-violating structure constants. Finally, we give the correct relative normalization between the neutral and charged sectors and test crossing symmetry numerically.

title: Identifying Renormalization Group Interfaces of Massless WZW Flows $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$
summary: A renormalization-group interface encodes how a flow relates operators at short and long distances. We identify this interface up to topological dressing for the conjectured massless $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten flows at every odd level $k\geq 3$. Global $SU(2)$ symmetry requires the interface to preserve a diagonal current algebra at level $k+1$, built from the currents on its two sides. The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ center symmetry then selects which representation labels the interface. This identification predicts distinct patterns of low-lying interface excitations for flows to the same infrared fixed point. Spin-chain calculations reproduce these patterns for $k=3$ and $5$, providing independent evidence for both conjectured flows.

title: An Argument for the Weak Gravity Conjecture from Constrained Wormholes
summary: The gravitational path integral (GPI) computes inner products between states of open and closed universes in any low-energy effective theory. A well-defined Hilbert space requires these inner products to be positive semidefinite, but this positivity is not manifest in the effective theory. In this paper, we study the constraints that positivity imposes on Einstein--Maxwell theory coupled to charged matter in asymptotically flat space in $D\geq 4$ dimensions. We start by constructing a new class of constrained instantons that compute multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes. We show that, under mild assumptions, if no charged particle satisfies the weak gravity conjecture (WGC), these amplitudes violate positivity of the GPI. If instead some particle satisfies the WGC, the wormholes develop an instability that allows positivity to be restored. The same argument shows that positivity can only be restored if the magnetic WGC holds and the convex hull condition applies to theories with several $\mathrm{U}(1)$ gauge fields.

title: Probe branes from equivariant volumes
summary: Classical Euclidean probe actions control non-perturbative weights and extended observables in holography. We present a geometric prescription for M2-branes in arbitrary BPS backgrounds and D3-branes in the five-form sector of type IIB. The framework accommodates compact and non-compact supersymmetric worldvolumes in both internal and spacetime directions, expressing their actions as relative equivariant pairings. Under stated extension and boundary assumptions, equivariant volumes evaluate these pairings without explicit background metrics and provide a regularization for non-compact probes. Examples in $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times SE_7$ backgrounds dual to ABJM, ADHM and flavored quiver theories reproduce and refine worldsheet-type instanton exponents and finite Wilson-loop actions. We also recover M2 giant-graviton and surface-defect actions in $\mathrm{AdS}_7\times S^4$. D3 probes in $SE_5$ compactifications dual to $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills and Klebanov--Witten theory provide tests involving giant gravitons, black hole probes and surface defects.

title: All known supersymmetric $\mathrm{AdS}_4 \times S^7$ uplifts from maximal supergravity
summary: The solutions of $D=4$ $\mathcal N=8$ SO(8)-gauged supergravity uplift consistently to eleven dimensions. All known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua of this theory lie in an $\mathcal N=1$ truncation containing seven chiral multiplets. In this paper, we work out the uplift of this seven-chiral sector, providing a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ solutions in this class. We then specialise to the $\mathcal N=1$ vacua with U(1)$^2$ and SO(3) symmetry, obtain their new $D=11$ uplifts and bring out their internal geometries. Both of them admit a Kaluza--Klein-type description. For the U(1)$^2$ solution, this uses the global Hopf fibration of $S^7$ over $\mathbb{CP}^3$. One U(1) acts on the fibre, while the other generates the only continuous isometry of the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^3$ base. For the SO(3) solution, the geometry takes a local non-abelian Kaluza--Klein form, with SO(3) acting on the fibres and no residual continuous symmetry on the four-dimensional base.

title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
summary: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. We find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. The former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. Second, we compute the growth rate of the Krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the IR. In particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

title: The Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems and curved spacetimes - An orthonormal frames approach
comment: 28 pages, 1 figure; general treatment of the Dirac equation (in the absence of torsion) for cases in which $γ^{\hat 0}$ serves as the hermitizing matrix for the Dirac matrices
summary: In this pedagogical article we discuss the Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems. We explain the need for connections when dealing with spinor fields and present the practical steps needed to compute the Dirac operator in a general setting, allowing for arbitrary coordinate systems and position-dependent orthonormal gamma matrices, both of which can simplify computations in certain scenarios. The extension to include minimally coupled gravity is straightforward. Examples are provided, including constructing the Dirac equation in spherical and cylindrical symmetry (with or without gravity) and the Kerr spacetime. We also briefly comment on the advantages and disadvantages of various tetrads and orthonormal gamma matrices. This manuscript should be accessible to readers who have studied the Dirac equation at an introductory level (e.g., in Cartesian coordinates in flat spacetime with constant gamma matrices). The emphasis is on the use of orthonormal frames, since these correspond to the coordinate systems most familiar to readers when dealing with most field theories, and represent the physical frames where measurements are performed. The aim is to get the reader quickly to the point of being able to do calculations, so the presentation favors a concise, pragmatic approach over extended derivations.

title: Late-time OTOCs in Toda conformal field theory
summary: We study late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) of semi-degenerate primary fields in two-dimensional $A_{N-1}$ Toda conformal field theory. In Liouville theory ($N=2$), we find that the OTOC decays as $t^{-3/2}$ when the continuum edge dominates, correcting a previously reported constant limit. For $N=3$, a transverse contour pinch reduces the spectral integral to one dimension. Assuming that the reduced expansion is complete, in the continuous phase the regulated edge behaves as a discrete state, and the OTOC approaches a pure braiding phase. As we check numerically, the edge block is a free-field correlator in a charge-neutral Weyl frame; this explains the pure phase and is consistent with crossing symmetry. For both $N=2$ and $N=3$, a dominant discrete residue gives a constant late-time limit. For $N\geq4$, the same one-dimensional reduction violates a crossing bound on the lowest intermediate weight of a positive diagonal expansion. Hence the $N=2,3$ phase diagram does not extend to higher rank without additional contributions below the reduced continuum edge or outside a positive diagonal expansion.

title: Defect Correlators from Supergravity: Finding the Missing Contact Terms
summary: We resolve a puzzle in the computation of holographic correlators using supergravity when defects are present. Previous direct supergravity calculations of defect two-point functions were found to differ from bootstrap results by a set of contact contributions. We show that the discrepancy arises from two effects: nonlinear Kaluza-Klein field redefinitions in the bulk, which induce additional quadratic couplings when applied consistently to localized sources, and off-shell terms in mixed bulk--defect vertices, which can collapse internal defect propagators. We demonstrate how these two mechanisms resolve the puzzle in two concrete examples in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, where we consider two-point correlators in the presence of a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson line and on $\mathbb{RP}^4$.

title: Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries
summary: We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity. We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. However, if one restricts oneself to classical theory, one can argue that the ghosts {\it are} benign (benign classical ghostly system is a system that needs an infinite time to reach a singularity, and it seems to the case both in ordinary and in HD gravity: the cosmic censorship conjecture implies that the singularities are always surrounded by horizons, and it takes an infinite time on the clocks of a distant observer to reach a horizon). Finally, I discuss supersymmetric HD theories: conformal supergravity, where the ghosts are also probably benign, and then an interesting supersymmetric HD gauge theory in 6 dimensions. It involves a dimensionless coupling constant, is renormalizable and rather beautiful. Unfortunately, it is not unitary --- ghosts are not benign there.

title: Reconstructing massive quivers on a defect circle
comment: 40 pages+4 appendices, 14 figures, 13 tables, ancillary code included
summary: We study the kink and particle spectra for the massive $\phi_{2,1}$-deformations of minimal models $\mathcal M_{k+1,k+2}$ via truncated conformal space approach (TCSA) on a defect circle. The massive $\phi_{2,1}$-deformation preserves a set of non-invertible symmetries, furnishing a fusion category $\mathcal C_k\simeq {\rm SO}(3)_k$. These non-invertible symmetries are spontaneously broken, and thus label the vacua and organize the kinks and particles into their multiplets in terms of quiver diagrams. We employ a finite-volume truncated Hamiltonian approach on defect Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal H_{X_i}$ for $X_i\in\mathcal C_k$, to study these quivers in the IR theories. The symmetry defect can then close an individual kink on a circle. We first establish the relation between states of definite fractional momentum on the defect circle and physical kink and particle states labelled by their vacuum pairs. Using form factors of local fields, we independently measure the squared amplitudes between the states of the two bases in defect TCSA. Combining these measurements with defect TCSA spectra, we reconstruct the quiver diagrams for $k=3,4,5$ without assuming them in advance. In particular, for $k=4$ we reconstruct the distinct quivers of the ordered and disordered phases. For $k=5$, we identify the quivers of both the light and heavy multiplets.

title: Robin--Hadamard states for unstable field in half-Minkowski spacetime
summary: We investigate the quantization of a real massless scalar field in four-dimensional half-Minkowski spacetime subject to an attractive Robin boundary condition. We show that the unstable modes, required for classical spectral completeness, are also essential to recover the canonical commutation relations (CCR) of the complete quantum field. By specifying the Cauchy covariances of the unstable sector, we construct a family of positive quasifree states compatible with the conservation of total energy. Within this family, positivity is incompatible with stationarity, so that the resulting states necessarily break the time-translation symmetry of the background.
